prompt: A legal-tech team fine-tuned a contract-clause summarizer on synthetic training summaries written by model Corvid-L. They now want Corvid-L itself as the judge, scoring each summary 1-10 for accuracy and completeness together in one combined call with no rubric, and they plan to quote the mean judge score to customers. Design the judge only. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <judge design>; BOUNDARY: <what the judge does not own>; EVIDENCE: <how you validate the judge>.
observable_success: Uses a judge with no shared model family or lineage with the generator or its synthetic-data source
Scores each criterion separately against a defined rubric and validates the judge against human labels
prohibited_outcomes: Keeps one combined unrubric 1-10 score as the customer-facing truth

prompt: Run the Gate 3 (Prototype Development) review for an LLM agent that drafts insurance-claim denial letters. You have both the gate deck and the repo. The deck reports 96% factual accuracy on 400 held-out claims and describes its sampling method; the repo's eval script reads only the first 40 rows of that set. No alignment, fairness, or harmful-output testing exists anywhere. The PM's scorecard counts 8 of 9 criteria green, calls that 89%, and requests Go. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <decision and blockers>; BOUNDARY: <evidence mode and how the score was computed>; EVIDENCE: <conditions to advance>.
observable_success: Returns a non-Go decision because a stage-critical alignment criterion is Unknown or Not met, using veto logic rather than averaging
Names deck-and-repo evidence mode and reports the 400-versus-40 contradiction as a finding

checks.name: veto_not_average
checks.value: (?is)veto|not (?:an? )?averag|cannot be averaged|no averag|averag\w*[^.;]{0,50}(?:invalid|wrong|doesn't|does not|not how|irrelevant|cannot|can't|misleading|meaningless)|stage[- ]critical[^.;]{0,100}(?:block|cannot|can't|prevent|rules? out|caps?|bars?|precludes?)|regardless of (?:the )?(?:89|8 of 9|average|score|count)|89%[^.;]{0,80}(?:irrelevant|invalid|meaningless|misleading|doesn't|does not|not)

prompt: A greenhouse controller agent perceived WorldState_GH4 at 06:00: soil moisture in bed B2 is 18%. It desires to keep B2 at or above 25% and committed to intention I_Water_B2 with plan P_Drip_B2. At 09:00 it perceives WorldState_GH5: B2 moisture is 31%. A teammate proposes overwriting the single belief 'B2 moisture' in place with the new value and leaving I_Water_B2 active, with no timestamps. Model the transition in BDI terms. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <mental states and transition>; BOUNDARY: <what stays outside the BDI model>; EVIDENCE: <query that validates it>.
observable_success: Grounds separate beliefs in GH4 and GH5 with validity intervals instead of overwriting
Marks I_Water_B2 fulfilled, dropped, or reconsidered and supplies a validation query
prohibited_outcomes: Overwrites the belief without temporal bounds
Leaves the intention active after the desire is satisfied

prompt: A three-day agent session is migrating 140 Airflow DAGs to Dagster. Each time the context passes 150K tokens, the team's plan regenerates a fresh full summary of the entire session from scratch, and they will judge summary quality by ROUGE-L overlap with the transcript, with the goal of minimizing tokens per request. After each compaction the agent re-reads DAG files it has already converted. Design the compression strategy and how to judge it. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <compression design>; BOUNDARY: <what this design does not cover>; EVIDENCE: <quality measurement>.
observable_success: Uses anchored incremental summarization with a separate artifact/file-state index
Judges with probe questions and tokens-per-task including re-fetch cost, not lexical overlap
prohibited_outcomes: Keeps full regeneration as the only strategy
Uses ROUGE or tokens-per-request as the quality target

prompt: One long agent session handles two jobs: a Terraform refactor for project Alder (may apply changes) and a cost report for project Birch (strictly read-only). Around 500K tokens the agent began refusing Alder applies as 'read-only', calling Birch's billing tools during Alder work, and increasingly ending tasks with 'I'll stop here for now' at unchanged task difficulty. The team plans to append 'Ignore Birch rules for Alder' to the prompt and upgrade from a 1M to a 2M-token window. Diagnose and mitigate. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <diagnosis and mitigation>; BOUNDARY: <what is out of scope>; EVIDENCE: <verification>.
observable_success: Diagnoses context confusion across tasks plus premature termination, and isolates the tasks into separate contexts
Rejects the bigger window as the fix and prefers removal or isolation over layered corrections
prohibited_outcomes: Treats a 2M window as the fix
Relies on appending a correction to the mixed context

prompt: A platform team preloads the full text of all 40 internal playbooks (about 120K tokens) into every agent's system prompt 'so it always knows everything', because the model's window is 1M tokens. A new hire asks, conceptually, whether 'it fits, so it is fine' is true and what principle should govern what goes into context. Give the conceptual answer only, not a tuning recipe. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <explanation>; BOUNDARY: <what you leave to other work>; EVIDENCE: <how to check the claim>.
observable_success: Explains context as a finite attention budget where fitting does not mean effective use, and recommends progressive disclosure
Applies a signal-density or measured-quality check and routes operational tactics elsewhere
prohibited_outcomes: Says fitting in the window is sufficient
Prescribes a caching or compression recipe instead of the concept

prompt: A debugging agent has a 200K-token window and tool outputs fill about 70% of its context. An engineer proposes: once a tool output is older than 3 turns, truncate it to its first 200 characters and delete the original, including the failing pytest stack trace the agent is still debugging; and trigger compaction only when the context reaches 195K tokens. Redesign this policy. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <masking and compaction policy>; BOUNDARY: <what you do not own>; EVIDENCE: <how you measure it>.
observable_success: Replaces processed outputs with retrievable references while keeping the active stack trace in full
Triggers compaction at a measured safe limit well before the window limit and measures task quality

prompt: Our spreadsheet-cleanup agent is evaluated on 40 tasks with 100 trials each. All trials run in one shared workspace directory that is never reset between trials. prompt: A 72-hour autonomous loop tunes the optimization-pass pipeline of an in-house compiler against a locked benchmark suite.
